o1.biggest_strength: Cash limit and the break-in note appear where buyers decide: bullet, button line, what-fits table and FAQ. It names the returns problem, quantifies it, then solves it in our calm voice.
o1.biggest_mistake: The opening strategy note and 'What to watch' read like an internal memo pasted onto a product page, which would need stripping before publishing.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the meta-commentary from the deliverable and add the front-pocket width/height if known.

o2.biggest_strength: The 'What fits, in real life' scenarios (light day, full day, the most it takes, what doesn't fit) are genuinely useful and on-brand for showing how it carries.
o2.biggest_mistake: Leaves the break-in point off the add-to-cart button line, so the highest-leverage return fix (snug for a week) is buried mid-page. Its gift FAQ also answers Jen but not Jen's 'look good in five years' doubt as sharply.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Put the break-in note in the button line, state the cash number in the subtitle, and tighten the FAQ to the actual top three questions.

reason: Both are strong and on-voice, but Output 1 aims every element at the 44% cash returns and 7.5% early tight-slot returns with the button line doing real work; Output 2 is charming and more readable in its scenarios but leaves the return-cutting line under the button generic.
